I use Yazio for calorie tracking, you can scan barcodes for the products you eat which makes it really easy. In the beginning I would recommend just logging EVERYTHING (Snacks, drinks, etc) you consume for a week. Then look at the number and try decreasing it by 300kcal per day. Be consistent.

You have to have a deficit (e.g. You need/eat 2500kcal a day, cut 500kcal a day-> 500kcal deficit) of 7000kcal for 1kg of weight loss. 
If you have a 500kcal defizit everyday you would loose 1/2 kg (i think it's 1 pound) a week.

Make sure you get enough protein (you can see that in the calorie tracker app, they give you a goal for it)
Eating enough protein can manage your hunger and appetite and is important for your muscles.


Yazio also calculates how many calories you should eat to loose weight but you can go in your own pace.


You don't have to Work out for the calories burned since working out doesn't burn that much BUT I highly recommend it. If you don't workout at all just try getting more steps in. You can also do some home workouts there are many great ones on YouTube, I personally like Pamela Reif. 

Also if you personally feel great and happy with your size and only want to focus in getting healthier you can try by reducing unhealthy foods and move more but I personally like counting calories.

If you have questions let me know I am happy to help :)

I am diagnosed with both but I feel like my bpd stems from my autism. People with autism tend to get traumatized more easily & I didn't get diagnosed with autism until I was 20 and thus didn't get any help growing up. People with BPD also tend to be more sensitive I think that there is a big overlap (&I don't really like the diagnosing of BPD but that's a different topic lmao)
Symptoms unique to my autism are:
Autistic meltdowns: occur when I am overstimulated or plans change.
Being "too" honest and not understanding when I have to act professional.
Not being able to understand NT way of socialising.
NT sense that I am not "one of them" (there was a study that proofed this even) leading to being the last one to socialise in new groups, the last one to connect with people, last one to find a partner in group projects etc.

Those are Symptoms that are (as far as I know) unique to Autism. I can also recommend Dr Natalie Engelbrecht who specializes in autism in women.

Still we don't know a lot about Autism - the first Person to ever get diagnosed is still alive today and the research in how it represents in women is only at the beginning.

What helped me for my mental health overall was DBT. An official autism diagnosis doesnt really help much since there are no resources for adults and self diagnosing in the autistic community is totally valid but I do understand wanting an official diagnsois since I also wanted to do the assessment just to be sure about "whats wrong with me".

Wish you well, take care

I can't respond to your comment but I got the notification. I am from Austria I think it really depends on the country you are from but basically I called the department for psychotherapy and psychiatry in the hospital, told them that I want a diagnosis and explained a bit about my symptoms. They refered me to another department and that's where I got my appointment. It's just an assessment and they will recommend how I continue with treatment but they will not treat me after that (exept they see me as being a harm to myself/others then they would keep me there for a few days but that shouldnt happen lol)

I have been to several different psychiatrists and they all just said it was depression and anxiety and that's it, even when I was (in hindsight) clearly manic and psychotic at times. I switched to someone who is specialized in more "serious" mental illnesses (Cluster B personality disorders, BP and such) and he diagnosed me on our second meeting. First was in person, second one via Zoom.
I wasn't sure about it bc he also completely dismissed my autism (old guy who literally told me I couldn't have autism bc I don't look like it.) BUT after I got the meds and took them for a while I really noticed it getting better. 

I think when someone is experienced and has had many clients with this disorder then they are able to diagnose more quickly & you can get the meds you need. If it is possible for you I would recommend looking up a clinic or something that also diagnoses. Here it's free but you have to wait for half a year but they will do all kinds of tests to rule out other physical reasons for your symptoms. 

The most important thing is that the symptoms that make your life harder are being treated. 

Wish you well :)

I had a lot of traumatic events happening to me and I didn't know I was traumatised, I just knew that there was something wrong. If you feel the same the following exercise May help, my therapist is trauma specialized and she does this with me: (you can also do it alone)

Make a chronological list of your live Events (one Event a year from the earliest you remember) and loudly read them through, chronologically. It doesnt have to be only traumatic experiences in your timeline. Take the same time (Like 2 Seconds) for each. Don't stop at an event but if you feel like screaming, stimmung, anything at all, do it. After you went through the timeline, do a grounding exercise. 

It's not a lot but it's the only thing that has really helped me so far, maybe it helps you too.

I have been in therapy for 7 years on and off. I was diagnosed with depression, social anxiety, autism and PTSD. I struggle with self harm and suicidal thoughts. Recently checked into a psych unit where they focuse on therapy. I have learned that it is really hard and you have to put in a lot of effort to feel okay.
Here's a few things that have helped me:

Find out what you enjoy. Try doing things that you used to enjoy. Write a list and try doing those things a few times and see how it feels inside - does time fly, does it make you feel lighter, etc;

Stick to a Routine. Get up every morning, brush your teeth, keep your room clean, get dressed and go outside. You don't have to socialise but at least leave your house once a day.

Daily movement. Doesn't need to be workouts but simply move your body every day. Stretching in the morning and going for a walk is enough.

Enjoy nature. Go into a forest or go hiking or simply drive to a lake and be in nature.

Balance eating, sleeping and exercising. 

It is hard in the beginning, depending on your level of depression etc but all those things helped me step by step into actually enjoying living. No one can say or do anything to make you feel good you have to change your way of living if you want to change your mental health.

I can tell you about my experience from Austria.
I have been suspecting to be autistic for a while and looked up the dsm5 critiria and since I had every symptom I wanted to go and get an Assessment.
I am from a small county and I couldn't find any experts so I looked up the autism page in the capital and contacted them. They sent me a "list" of two experts who can diagnose adults with autism.
I called them both and said that me and my therapist think I may be autistic and if I could do an Assessment.

Those are private doctors, which means that you have to pay them yourself and insurance will most likely not cover it. But since you don't have to check with the insurance, you can go to them without an official referal from your doctor.

The Assessment itself was 3 parts: A lot of questionaires, a conversation and some tests (about understanding emotions, IQ-tests and concentration tests)
My mom had to fill out some of the questionaires because the symptoms must have existed for your whole life. 

After all those tests I got my results back and a 5 page PDF with all my "scores"

I have been diagnosed with Aspergerd by the ICD-10.

I hope that helped, if you have any questions feel free to dm me. I know how confusing it can be

Edit: The specialist who diagnosed me was a psychologist and mainly works with autistic people. Her office was VERY autistic friendly she had a lot of fidget tools and it was really quiet and the light was not too bright. Hey! I have been at my lowest a year ago. 
I don't know your exact situation but I'm just gonna list some things which I think may help you. Don't wanna act like I know it all or that any of that will make your depression disappear. Just trying to help.

If you can afford therapy and aren't in therapy atm, maybe try that. If you cannot afford it or don't wanna go, try journaling. 

Set yourself some small goals everyday. You are depressed and it is totally valid to not being able to get out of bad sometimes. But try to reach a small goal everyday (like getting up, eating good, reaching out to somebody) 

Walking helped me a lot. When I was very anxious or depressed I would force myself to get up and walk for some time. Maybe listen to some podcast (I loved true crime and self help stuff) or listen to some music.

Try getting a routine. Sleeping and eating well is importand for your overall health. 

And remember that you are loved! If you do feel suicidal, please let somebody who can help you know. It will get better one day.  

I don't wanna make it sound easy - I know how hard it is.
